Tahsin Ahmed Chowdhury

Trustworthy and Data-Efficient Computer Vision

North Western University · Khulna, Bangladesh

I am a Lecturer in Computer Science and Engineering at North Western University, Bangladesh, working where computer vision, medical imaging and federated learning meet. I build reliable, privacy-preserving machine learning for real-world healthcare, and I love turning real-life problems into research.

Research Interests

Four threads with one question underneath them: can a model be trusted with a decision that matters?

Medical Image AnalysisComputer Vision Conformal PredictionFederated Learning Explainable AIUncertainty Quantification Health InformaticsEmpirical Software Engineering

Medical image analysis

Detection and classification across histopathology, B-mode ultrasound and panoramic radiographs. Architecture designed against measured failure modes rather than generic attention, and models that stay clinically auditable instead of merely accurate.

HistopathologyUltrasoundRadiographs

Calibrated uncertainty

Distribution-free uncertainty quantification and conformal calibration used inside training, not only as a post-hoc report. The question underneath: how reliably do confidence estimates reflect errors on unfamiliar data?

ConformalCoverageCalibration

Federated learning

Learning under label scarcity, non-IID heterogeneity and sensing cost, on data that is hard to centralise because of privacy, governance or institutional rules — and the robustness of federated training itself.

Non-IIDAggregationRobustness

Empirical software engineering

Evaluation methodology, dataset construction and metric design for LLM-generated code. How do you show that a generated diff is actually better, rather than merely different from the one Git would produce?

LLMs for codeMiningMetrics

Research Projects

Selected projects, ongoing studies, and my contributions.

SAGE-YOLO26

Ultrasound lesion detection

Supervisor: Dr. Anupam Kumar Bairagi

Role
Project lead
Status
Manuscript in preparation

Developing a detector for spinal cord hematoma localisation in B-mode ultrasound. The approach incorporates ultrasound-specific signal characteristics, including speckle, depth-dependent attenuation, and lesion geometry. Evaluation uses animal-disjoint splits and controlled comparisons to assess the contribution of each component.

UltrasoundYOLO26WaveletsPyTorch

FedSense-OnDemand

Resource-aware wearable sensing

With Hirak Mondal · Supervisors: Dr. Mrinal Kanti Baowaly, Dr. Anupam Kumar Bairagi

Role
Project lead
Status
Under review · Machine Learning with Applications (Elsevier)

Developing a personalised federated framework for human activity recognition that requests additional sensor inputs when their expected benefit justifies the sensing cost. The study examines accuracy, uncertainty, and resource use when clients have different sensors or missing modalities.

WearablesFederatedMultimodalCalibration

LLM-generated diffs

Empirical evaluation

Supervisor: Dr. Yusuf Sulistyo Nugroho · Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta

Role
Project lead
Status
Under review · Empirical Software Engineering

Leading an empirical comparison of LLM-generated diffs and Git’s histogram algorithm across 14 open-source repositories. My work includes dataset construction and the design of statistical and human evaluation protocols. A related study examines how generated diffs affect R-SZZ bug-introducing-change identification.

Empirical SELLMs for codeDatasetR-SZZ

FedCPS

Conformal calibration for federated learning

Supervisor: Dr. Anupam Kumar Bairagi

Role
Project lead
Status
In progress

Investigating conformal calibration for selecting pseudo-labels in federated semi-supervised learning. The project combines calibration across clients with a communication-efficient quantile aggregation protocol, and examines how client heterogeneity and repeated model updates affect coverage and pseudo-label reliability.

ConformalFederatedMedMNISTCIFAR

XFT-ViT · BBLRD

Efficient adaptation for histopathology

Extension of my undergraduate thesis

Role
Project lead
Status
In progress

Extending my undergraduate thesis through Backward Block Learning Rate Decay, a block-wise fine-tuning strategy for Vision Transformers. The project examines classification performance and training efficiency for lung and colon histopathology using LC25000 and LungHist-700.

HistopathologyViT-B/16Fine-tuning

Layer-wise ViT attention

Attention across layers in lung histopathology

Undergraduate thesis · Supervisor: Dr. Mrinal Kanti Baowaly

Role
Project lead
Status
Under review · 29th ICCIT

Investigating how attention changes across Vision Transformer layers during lung histopathology classification. The study compares attention visualisations with GradCAM++, SHAP, and LIME, alongside CNN baselines trained under matched protocols. This work formed my undergraduate thesis and is currently under review.

Explainable AISHAPGradCAM++LIME

About Me

Who I am, how I came to this work, and the standard I hold it to.

Biography

I am a Lecturer in Computer Science and Engineering at North Western University in Khulna, Bangladesh. I completed my B.Sc. in CSE at Gopalganj Science and Technology University, Bangladesh, graduating first in my cohort with a CGPA of 3.66/4.00.

My research began with lung cancer histopathology, comparing Vision Transformers with CNN baselines and examining attention across transformer layers. I am extending this work through XFT-ViT and Backward Block Learning Rate Decay, while exploring ultrasound lesion detection, conformal calibration for federated learning, and resource-aware learning for wearable sensing.

A separate research collaboration, developed during my internship at Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta, investigates how LLM-generated code changes differ from conventional tools and affect downstream software analysis.

Alongside research, I teach machine learning, computer vision, digital image processing, and data communication, and supervise undergraduate projects. I also support student research and higher-study preparation as an Associate Advisor to the GSTU Research and Higher Studies Society.

I hope to develop learning methods whose performance, uncertainty, and limitations can be evaluated clearly in realistic settings.

Research Internship and Cultural Exchange

Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta, Indonesia · Aug – Sep 2025

Indonesia, 2025

Host
Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta (UMS)
Supervisor
Dr. Yusuf Sulistyo Nugroho
Funding
Fully funded

Straight after my B.Sc. final examinations, I was offered a fully funded research internship and cultural exchange in Indonesia, hosted by Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta (UMS). Working alongside faculty from UMS and the Nara Institute of Science and Technology (NAIST), Japan, I explored current trends and open research questions in empirical software engineering, shared my own ideas and learned from theirs.

A highlight was the chance to discuss my work one to one, and collaborate, with Prof. Dr. Kenichi Matsumoto of NAIST, an internationally recognised software-engineering researcher, and to hear his view of where the field is heading. Between research sessions, the programme opened the door to Javanese culture, from batik workshops to temple visits.
